title: Biotech Catalyst Trading: How Hedge Funds and Insiders Position Around FDA Decisions | BiopharmaWatch
snippet:
One of the most well-documented patterns in biotech is the "PDUFA run-up." In the weeks leading up to a PDUFA date, biotech stocks tend to move higher as traders and investors build positions ahead of the binary event.
...
- Speculative buying. Traders who want to bet on approval start building positions 4 to 8 weeks before the decision date.
- Hedge fund accumulation. Professional investors who have done deep diligence and have conviction in the drug quietly accumulate shares over weeks, trying not to push the price up too fast.
- Short covering. If the stock had been heavily shorted, some shorts start covering their positions ahead of the binary event to limit their risk, which pushes the price higher.
- Momentum traders. Once the stock starts moving up, momentum-based algorithms and traders jump in, accelerating the run-up.
- Options activity. Increased call option buying ahead of PDUFA dates can create a "gamma squeeze" effect as market makers hedge their exposure by buying shares.
...
| Timeframe | What Usually Happens | Trading Implication |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 to 6 weeks out | Smart money starts quietly building positions. Volume may tick up slightly. | Best time to enter if you are playing the run-up. Stock is not yet "crowded." |
| 6 to 4 weeks out | The move becomes more noticeable. Media coverage and analyst notes increase. | Run-up is underway. Still time to enter, but risk-reward is less favorable. |
| 4 to 2 weeks out | Volume spikes. Options premiums surge.

title: How to Trade PDUFA Dates — Biotech Catalyst Trading Strategy | Dan Sfera
snippet:
Investors

 PDUFA dates are the sharpest binary events in all of equities. A single FDA decision can double a stock or cut it in half before the close. Here's how experienced biotech traders approach these events — including the traps that kill most retail investors who try to play them blind.
...
Most stock-moving events — earnings, analyst upgrades, macro data — play out on a spectrum. PDUFA dates don't. The FDA delivers one of three verdicts: Approved, Complete Response Letter (CRL), or Extension. For small-cap biotechs where the drug under review is the entire pipeline, that decision determines whether the company survives. 

 This binary structure is why PDUFA stocks behave differently from the rest of the market: 

The "PDUFA Pop" Pattern

 In the weeks and days leading up to a PDUFA date, traders and institutions accumulate positions in anticipation of approval. This pre-approval run-up — often called the "PDUFA pop" or "PDUFA drift" — can be 20–100% above where the stock was 90 days out. When the approval comes, the initial gap is often smaller than the run-up that preceded it. When the CRL comes, the gap down hits a stock that was already trading on hope.
...

title: How Biotech Stocks Move Around FDA Decisions: Data on 60+ PDUFA Events
snippet:
Across 64 FDA decision dates with price data, biotech stocks moved an average of -1.8% on the decision day and -4.4% over the following five trading days. Stocks rose an average of +2.6% in the 30 days before the decision, then 52% closed lower on the day itself — the classic "run-up then fade" pattern. The average absolute move was 9.1%, and single events ranged from +41.5% to -70.7%.
...
Most FDA decision days are quieter than headlines suggest — but the tails are brutal. Of 64 events:

Surged +20% or more 3 (5%) Up +5% to +20% 11 (17%) Flat (within ±5%) 37 (58%) Down -5% to -20% 9 (14%) Dropped -20% or more 4 (6%)

58% of decisions landed within ±5%, yet roughly 1 in 9 events moved more than 20% in one direction. FDA decisions are high-variance, not one-directional.
